title: Story: Roll out Original / Remastered card-image buttons, saved defaults and language-aware availability across the wiki
body:
## User story
As a wiki reader, I want to choose Original or Remastered images for the card I am viewing and save my default, so that I can favor historical source images or readability without confusing card versions or languages.

## Bill's approved direction — 14 November 2026
Bill approved the simplified #429 pilot and the labels **Original / Remastered**, requested this rollout Story including saved defaults and translation behavior, and then corrected placement and visibility:
> “the Button should be BELOW the card images”
> “I meant Buttons: Original and Remastered. Those buttons only show if the card itself has more than one version.”

Here, image versions are renditions of the **same selected card publication/text state and card-image language**. They are not different errata, printings or gameplay identities. The buttons appear as a pair only when that card has both Original and Remastered renditions available. Multiple unrelated card articles, another card's remaster, or multiple historical scans alone do not create this pair.

This Story specifies the requested wiki rollout. The currently deployed #429 pilot is the starting point; its above-image placement is superseded by the below-images requirement here. Creating/readying this Story does not claim that rollout or preference behavior is implemented.

## Requirements
R1. Roll the shared image-selection behavior out across eligible wiki card articles and card-image panels, for Decipher and Virtual eras. Inventory shared card-image consumers, including set-table thumbnails and hover views; keep their compact presentation while making image resolution consistent with the selected card state/language and reader preference. Scope the controls to the actual card panel, not decorative images or a duplicate control beside every thumbnail.

R2. Use thin, readable, text-only **Original** and **Remastered** buttons. Use the approved 26px-high pilot as the desktop baseline and retain usable keyboard/touch targets. **Position the pair below the complete card-image group**, above the Info table where present: selected full-card image → publisher slip, if applicable → Original / Remastered buttons → Info. Do not put the buttons above the card or between the full card and its slip. No preview thumbnails in buttons, under-image captions or Compare control/dialog.

R3. Show both buttons only when two distinct eligible image renditions exist for that specific selected card and image language: an Original and a matching Remastered. With only one rendition, display it without either button, a disabled alternative, empty space or a sitewide toggle masquerading as a card option. Recompute availability when card version or card language changes. A missing/broken asset must degrade usefully rather than leave a blank image or nonfunctional switcher.

R4. Switching image rendition changes presentation only. Keep the same publication/text state, card ID, lore/game text/stats/icons and language; retain the matching publisher slip immediately below the selected full card. Preserve original bytes and accessible File/provenance links. Original means the historical source image of this version: it may be a printed scan, publisher slip or historical constructed composite. Keep the actual source/creator in article/File provenance; a Holotable composite is not thereby an official printed full card. Do not pair a remaster of another errata state or printing just to enable the buttons.

R5. Add a clear **Card images: Original / Remastered** saved-default preference outside the repeated card panels. Initial default is Original. Signed-in preferences persist with the account across sessions/devices; guest preferences persist in that browser. Buttons provide the current card's selection; the explicit saved-default setting controls future default selections. Switching a card does not silently rewrite the saved global default. An account preference takes precedence after sign-in; signing out must not copy that account's setting into another guest's browser preference. Unavailable/blocked storage, an unset/invalid preference or a preference API failure must leave a usable card view.

R6. If the preferred rendition is unavailable, show the available rendition of the **same selected card state and language** without buttons. Keep the stored preference for other eligible cards; do not substitute another printing, errata state, card or language to satisfy it. For a card with no usable image, retain the wiki's honest missing-image behavior and no buttons.

R7. Treat wiki interface language, card-image language and image rendition as separate choices. Do not hide the feature merely because the wiki interface is translated. Localize controls/settings through the wiki's language mechanism. If only a translated remaster exists in the selected card language, show it alone without the pair; if both matching same-language renditions exist, show both buttons and honor the saved preference. Historical foreign-language printed cards follow the same availability rule. Do not silently use an English Original as an Original in another language or invent a historical translation.

R8. Preserve responsive layout, selected-state semantics, focus/keyboard behavior and useful no-JavaScript fallback. Avoid duplicate initialization and layout shifts between renditions. Reading or writing a preference must not leak account state through shared anonymous page caches. Preserve current publication/version navigation, image provenance, and gameplay eligibility policies.

R9. Deploy and audit in controlled batches with merged source, rollback, per-batch coverage/gap records, source accuracy checks, exact independent backups and required publication/preservation registration. Retain the team-wide Archive.org hold: no requests to archive.org/web.archive.org until Bill explicitly lifts it; only the existing central owner resumes preservation. Registered/backed-up images are not externally preserved by implication. Missing remasters are coverage gaps, not a requirement to manufacture all of them in this Story.

## Acceptance criteria and verification
- [ ] AC1 **Placement/appearance:** representative Decipher and Virtual articles have readable text-only Original/Remastered buttons below all their card images, after the slip where present and before Info. No old preview/caption/Compare UI remains. Desktop/mobile screenshots and DOM geometry assertions prove order.
- [ ] AC2 **Availability:** original-only, remaster-only, both available, no image, broken asset and another-card/another-state-only alternatives all behave as R3/R6 specify. No pair is shown merely because a family has multiple gameplay versions or another language has a remaster. Save the fixture/availability matrix.
- [ ] AC3 **Exact-state invariants:** switching either way preserves the selected card publication/text state, ID, article text and matching slip. Include errata/pre-errata, different printing/border, and historical composite + slip cases; reject mismatched alternatives. Record source mappings and checks.
- [ ] AC4 **Saved defaults:** account preference survives session/device changes; guest choice survives reload/navigation in that browser; explicit setting and per-card selection behave distinctly. Verify sign-in/account precedence, sign-out isolation, new users, invalid values and storage/API failures. Shared anonymous caches do not serve another reader's preference or account data.
- [ ] AC5 **Fallback:** a saved preference unavailable on one card shows the available same-language/state rendition without controls or a blank, retains the preference, and uses it on the next eligible card. No-image behavior stays honest. Test version/language changes and image-load failure.
- [ ] AC6 **Translations:** verify translated interface + English images; translated remaster only; both same-language renditions; historical foreign-language Original only; both available after language change. The pair depends on image availability, not interface locale; localized labels/settings work; no silent language substitution.
- [ ] AC7 **Interaction/shared consumers:** keyboard selection/focus and assistive selected-state semantics work; touch/mobile fit without horizontal overflow; no-JavaScript fallback is useful; initialization is idempotent. Shared thumbnail/hover consumers retain compact layout and resolve the matching preferred image consistently, with no duplicate per-thumbnail buttons or effects on non-card images.
- [ ] AC8 **Rollout evidence:** inventory all affected templates/consumers and card coverage, explicitly separating eligible pairs, single-rendition cards, missing images and excluded mismatches. Each batch has required checks, own review, merged PRs, live verification, exact restorable backups, preservation/hold continuations and tested rollback. Record PASS-REPORT v1 mapped to all AC; do not call the whole wiki complete after one sample or call held preservation complete.

## Implementation plan
Inventory existing shared templates/image metadata, #429 code, preference mechanisms, localization and card-image consumers before changing them. Define one exact-card/state/language rendition resolver and explicit availability metadata; reuse working pilot code while removing its hardcoded Vader/exact-title assumptions. Implement the below-images panel and saved-default setting, then verify the acceptance matrix on sandbox/staging samples before controlled live batches. Coordinate #362/#364/#365 and #171; preserve their ownership and scope.

Repositories/files: billbisco/swccg-wiki shared card templates/application assets, preference/localization code and image metadata; existing image backup/catalog repositories; swccg-guild/work design log and evidence/<story>/. Use separate source/evidence checkouts and an isolated implementation branch. Split implementation batches into linked Tasks if needed; do not duplicate the pilot, remaster production or translation backlog. Any actual server configuration, database or permission change must follow its own applicable approval requirement; none is authorized by Story creation.

Verification maps directly to AC1–AC8 above; save the availability/language/preference fixture matrix, source mappings, browser checks, cache/isolation evidence, coverage report, snapshots and rollback results. Principal risks are mismatched text states, global-versus-per-card preference confusion, language substitution, shared-cache leakage, duplicate consumers and active card editors.

## Related work and scope boundaries
Parent: #165 (card/version preservation). Starting point: #429, source PR38 in billbisco/swccg-wiki. Coordinate #364 (leading publication), #365 (matching Decipher remasters), #362 (Original Set1 history), #171 (translation/localization), #419 (Holotable sources), and #403 (wiki launch planning). Link rollout disposition to launch planning without declaring it a launch blocker or changing the launch decision.

Out of scope: generating every missing remaster/translation, modifying historical originals, changing card text/errata/identities or formats, changing GEMP's image defaults, new global card-version policy, and resuming Archive.org access. This is a rendition preference within the chosen card version, not a replacement for Versions navigation.

## Open questions
None blocking the requested Story. Bill approved Original / Remastered and the proposed preference/translation behavior, then specified below-images placement and per-card availability. Routine implementation choices should follow these testable requirements. Any genuinely unresolved scope/permission decision discovered during implementation goes on this ticket before dependent work.
